title: Words a Broken Keyboard Can Type
statement:
Some keys on a keyboard are broken. You get a string text of lowercase words separated by single spaces (no spaces at the ends), and a string brokenLetters holding the distinct lowercase letters whose keys do not work. It may be empty.

Return how many words of text can be typed in full, that is, how many words contain none of the broken letters.

examples.why: Only "dog" needs the broken o key.
No key is broken, so every word works.
"noon" holds two o's but is still just one lost word. Counting broken letters in the text and subtracting would go wrong.

constraints: text is lowercase words separated by single spaces

args: caa e ad d d b

hints: A word is either typable or not. What single question decides it?
A word fails if any of its letters is broken. Checking membership of a letter is fastest with a set.
Put the broken letters in a set, split the text on spaces, and count the words where no letter is in the set.

explain.intuition:
Each word is a yes-or-no question: does it contain any broken letter? Put the broken letters in a set so each check is O(1), then walk the words and count the ones that pass. It is the same check as validating an input against a list of forbidden characters.

You can also do it in one pass over the characters without splitting: keep a flag "current word is broken". Set it when you meet a broken letter, and at every space (and at the end) count the word if the flag is clear, then reset it.
steps: For each word, check whether every letter is outside the set.
Count the words that pass and return the count.
pitfalls: Counting broken letters instead of broken words. "noon" has two o's but costs one word.
Splitting an empty brokenLetters into [""] and then testing word.includes(""), which is always true and blocks every word.
In the one-pass version, forgetting to count the last word, which has no space after it.

complexity.space: O(|text|) for the split, O(1) for the one-pass version

solutions.title: Split and check with a set
solutions.idea: Store the broken letters in a set and count the words that use none of them.

solutions.title: One pass with a flag
solutions.idea: Walk the characters, remember whether the current word hit a broken key, and settle it at each space and at the end.

followups: Return the typable words themselves, in order.
Each broken key can still be pressed, but costs 3 extra seconds. Which words can be typed within a time budget per word?
lcTitle: Maximum Number of Words You Can Type
